text: Fresh brownie and a smoothie for the road.
notes: Two single words as written.

text: Start your morning with an espresso and a croissant.
notes: Two single words as written.

text: Homemade lemonade is back for the summer.
notes: One word as written.

text: Warm apple crumble with custard, only on Sundays.
notes: One word as written.

text: Blueberry muffins, fresh every morning.
notes: Plural.

text: Stacks of pancakes with maple syrup, all day.
notes: Plural.

text: We now have three kinds of tarts at the counter.
notes: Plural of an ambiguous word, used in the pastry sense. 'At the counter' is not the four word entry.

text: Brownies and smoothies are half price after six.
notes: Two plurals.

text: Try our new iced green tea this week.
notes: Three word entry; tea on its own is a tuned entry and counts as extra.

text: Cold brew coffee, steeped for eighteen hours.
notes: Three word entry; coffee on its own counts as extra. 'Cold coffee' is a tuned entry but the words are not next to each other.

text: Buy one get one on every muffin, Fridays only.
notes: Four word entry plus a single word.

text: Kids eat free every Sunday lunch.
notes: Three word entry.

text: Please pay at the counter before you take a seat.
notes: Four word entry with two stop words inside it.

text: Live music night with acoustic covers from 8 pm.
notes: Three word entry.

text: Pet friendly seating is now open on the terrace.
notes: Three word entry.

text: Show your student discount card at the till.
notes: Three word entry; discount on its own is a tuned entry and counts as extra.

text: Early bird offer: a free croissant before 9 am.
notes: Three word entry plus a single word.

text: Happy hour runs from 4 to 6 every weekday.
notes: Two word entry, the length the tuned glossary already had.

text: Our gluten-free bread is made fresh every day.
notes: Hyphen in the post, none in the entry; bread on its own counts as extra.

text: Free Wi-Fi for everyone, just ask for the password.
notes: The post writes Wi-Fi, the entry wifi.

text: Fresh croisants every morning.
notes: One letter missing, and plural.

text: Mango smoothy for the hot afternoons.
notes: Misspelt ending.

text: Join us for hapy hour, 4 to 6 pm.
notes: One letter missing inside a phrase.

text: The early bird ofer ends this Friday.
notes: One letter missing inside a three word phrase.

text: Try our hotcakes with fresh berries.
notes: Hotcakes are pancakes; nothing lexical can find that.

text: Our nimbu pani is back for the summer.
notes: Nimbu pani is lemonade.

text: BOGO on all brownies this Saturday.
notes: BOGO is buy one get one; brownie is a plural.

text: Buttered toast with strawberry jam, every morning.
notes: Both ambiguous words in the sense the glossary means.

text: Add an extra shot to any espresso drink.
notes: Shot in the espresso sense.

text: Lemon tart and a slice of apple pie, both baked today.
notes: Tart and pie in the glossary's sense; baked needs the tuned entry bake, as in the tuned set.

text: Stuck in a traffic jam? We will keep your table.
notes: A traffic jam, not fruit jam. Nothing should be injected.

text: Let's raise a toast to five years of the café!
notes: Raising a toast, not bread. Nothing should be injected.

text: Our new lime soda is a little tart, in a good way.
notes: Tart as in sour, not the pastry. Nothing should be injected.

text: This pie chart shows our most loved drinks.
notes: A pie chart. Nothing should be injected.

text: Great shot of the team at the food festival!
notes: A photo, not an espresso shot. Nothing should be injected.

text: This site uses cookies to remember your basket.
notes: Browser cookies: a tuned entry in a sense the tuned set never had. Nothing should be injected.
